name: Triodanis
look_here_first: LOOK FIRST at the whole leafy stem, especially how the UPPER LEAVES clasp the stem, then the ripe CAPSULE and its tiny seed-release WINDOW. Individual purple five-lobed flowers identify the group but seldom the species. Lower axils may contain closed (cleistogamous) flowers. Four accepted species plus one perfoliata subspecies from the five pool names.
shared_traits: Small annual herbs, one blue-violet 5-lobed flower at a leaf axil (not a composite capitulum)
Simple alternate leaves; attachment/clasping is variable
Inferior ovary becomes a many-seeded capsule with lateral dehiscence openings
Small closed selfing flowers (cleistogamous) can occur below showy upper open flowers
taxonomy_note: Triodanis biflora is accepted as Triodanis perfoliata subsp. biflora under Kew and ITIS.

genus_diagnostics.flower: Single fused corolla with five blue-violet lobes, usually fairly symmetric; five stamens are free, unlike Lobelia's anther tube.
genus_diagnostics.leaves: Simple alternate; full leaf bases may clasp the stem strongly in typical perfoliata or be less-clasping in biflora. Photograph several nodes.
genus_diagnostics.fruit: Inferior multi-seeded poricidal capsule; dehiscence pore commonly nearer middle in typical T. perfoliata and nearer tip in subsp. biflora; intermediate and hybrid forms occur. Photograph mature fruit side-on and use several structures, not a single ratio.
genus_diagnostics.stem: Small slender annual stems. Upper open (chasmogamous) and lower closed (cleistogamous) flowers may occupy different nodes.
genus_diagnostics.habit: Open-ground annual bellflower relatives; compare whole stem, not blossom color alone.

lookalikes.difference: Bilabiate asymmetrical 2+3 corolla and joined anthers into a tube; Triodanis usually radial blue-violet stars and free stamens.
Composite many-floret head rather than one five-lobed fused corolla.

visual_comparison.title: Triodanis — leaves and capsule windows first
visual_comparison.subtitle: Five nonempty licensed photographs physically checked across two taxon concepts; photos teach corolla, leaf base and closed flower. Three other accepted species still await exact media. Capsule window macros remain missing.
visual_comparison.memory_rule: BROAD CLASPING LEAVES + MIDDLE WINDOW → typical perfoliata; LESS CLASPING + TIP WINDOW → biflora. Others need matched capsule shape.

part_examples.title: Look at the open five-lobed corolla
part_examples.look_for: One blue-violet open corolla has five spreading lobes. This is a single flower, not an Asteraceae flower head.
part_examples.why_it_matters: Recognize the genus's basic flower form; neither color nor petal count alone settles the species.

part_examples.title: Find the clasping upper leaves
part_examples.look_for: Inspect the points where upper leaves attach to the stem; the broad leaf bases of typical clasping-looking-glass partly wrap the stem.
part_examples.why_it_matters: Leaf base is more useful than flower color for comparison with the biflora subspecies.

part_examples.title: See five violet corolla lobes up close
part_examples.look_for: This Bastrop County photograph is a FRONT MACRO of one open flower: five violet lobes and a pale central opening. Do not use it to judge leaf attachment or a capsule pore; neither is visible clearly here.
part_examples.why_it_matters: Shows that a flower close-up is not the same as a full-stem identification or seed-capsule diagnosis.

part_examples.title: Examine a flower from the side
part_examples.look_for: Purple five-lobed flowers attach to short green calyx/hypanthium structures at leaf axils. This shows real flower placement; it is not a dissected inferior ovary or a verified capsule pore.
part_examples.why_it_matters: Connects the star flower to its green supporting structure and stem node.

part_examples.title: Find a closed self-pollinating flower
part_examples.look_for: The small unopened floral structure is a self-pollinating cleistogamous flower, not a missing petal of the large showy bloom. Low-resolution image: zoom cautiously.
part_examples.why_it_matters: Many plants bear both open and inconspicuous closed flowers on the same shoot.

part_examples.title: Photograph the capsule window
part_examples.look_for: On a ripe green-brown capsule under a calyx, locate the actual lateral opening. Record whether it lies near the middle or close to the top; photo and scale not installed.
part_examples.why_it_matters: The most helpful tie-breaker between typical perfoliata and subsp. biflora.

part_examples.title: Find the inferior ovary
part_examples.look_for: Look at flower from side: the swollen ovary sits BELOW the calyx and corolla attachment. A matched true side macro is still needed.
part_examples.why_it_matters: The shared Campanulaceae family reproductive plan.

part_examples.title: Rare-species fruit and flower comparisons
part_examples.look_for: Obtain exact-species upper and lower leaf nodes, full narrow hypanthium, open flower and mature pore-bearing fruit for each of the three rare source taxa.
part_examples.why_it_matters: Their flowers alone can look nearly identical; no wrong-species substitute.

field_study_sequence: 1. Photograph the full stem including leaves toward the base and the top.
2. Magnify the upper leaf attachments: heart-shaped clasping or narrower less-clasping?
3. Find an individual five-lobed bloom and its swollen inferior ovary beneath the calyx.
4. Find an actually ripe capsule and the real pore; note location on capsule with a millimeter scale.
5. Check whether low nodes bear tiny closed flowers while upper nodes hold open blooms.
6. Compare species only when enough stem, fruit and flower evidence is visible.

quick_key.if: Broad upper leaves strongly clasp stem; capsule pore around middle in typical concept
Upper leaves often less-clasping; pore toward capsule tip
quick_key.then: T. perfoliata subsp. biflora (source 'T. biflora') likely

quick_key.if: Long narrow hypanthium, narrow upper bracts, elongated ribbed stem
quick_key.then: Compare T. coloradoensis vs T. leptocarpa with voucher/measurements

quick_key.if: Eastern Texas source name, no exact diagnostic fruit photos
quick_key.then: T. texana needs specialist photo review

comparison_matrix.coloradoensis: Narrower upper bracts; tapered lower leaves
comparison_matrix.leptocarpa: Narrow upper bracts and stem leaves

comparison_matrix.perfoliata: Pore often middle in typical subspecies
comparison_matrix.coloradoensis: Very narrow hypanthium; measured photo needed

taxonomy_notes: Source Triodanis biflora maps to accepted Triodanis perfoliata subsp. biflora; don't double count.
Native Texas state-wide does not certify project 3-county nativity.
No realistic confirmed arrows until exact pore and stamen position visually checked.

Morphological separation between typical T. perfoliata and source-name T. biflora can be complicated by hybrid/intermediate plants. Pore position is generally middle versus apical, not an infallible trait in all individuals.
diagnostic_photo_checklist: Actual pore-window closeups with annotated verified location for both subspecies
Full shoot/clasping leaf junctions at matched scale
Coloradoensis, leptocarpa and texana whole-plant and mature capsule photos, licensed
Inferior ovary calyx side macro, pollen and stamens
Do not duplicate unrelated T. biflora as an accepted separate species
